articles.headline: Mikel Arteta signs new four-year Arsenal contract
articles.description: Mikel Arteta has signed a new contract to extend his stay at Arsenal, the Premier League champions confirmed.
articles.headlineJa: ミケル・アルテタ、アーセナルと4年間の新契約を締結
articles.descriptionJa: プレミアリーグ覇者のアーセナルは、ミケル・アルテタが残留を決める新契約に署名したことを発表した。
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta has signed a new contract to extend his stay at Arsenal until 2030, the Premier League champions confirmed. 

ESPN previously reported that Arteta was set to pen a new contract. His previous deal was due to expire at the end of this season. 

The Spaniard led Arsenal to their first Premier League title in 23 years last season and also won the FA Cup in 2020. 

"It's a privilege to commit my future to the club and to continue to work with exceptional people who want the best for Arsenal," he said in a statement.

"This club is unique, its character and the way it makes you feel, and I have a great sense of privilege that our journey together will continue.

"We have already built a special bond and created memories that will last a lifetime, and what is so exciting is that this is only the beginning of what we can achieve together."

He joined the club in December 2019 after serving as assistant manager at Manchester City, and is currently the longest-serving head coach in the Premier League. 

Co-chairs Stan and Josh Kroenke said: "It has been an incredible journey so far and we are excited for what lies ahead in this special relationship. Last season was an incredible moment in Arsenal's history, a moment in which we created memories that will last a lifetime. We're determined to create many more in the years ahead.

"We share a special bond with Mikel. We are so proud of everything we have achieved since he returned to the club in 2019."

Arsenal have also confirmed that Arteta's coaching staff have also renewed their deals for four more years.

articles.headline: Fantasy football matchup rankings: Upgrade D'Andre Swift, fade James Cook III
articles.description: The most and least favorable matchups in the NFL for this week's games at the four key fantasy positions.
articles.headlineJa: ファンタジー・フットボール対戦カード評価：D・アンドレ・スウィフトを推奨、ジェームズ・クック3世は回避
articles.descriptionJa: 今週のNFLの試合における、ファンタジーの主要4ポジションの最も有利な対戦カードと最も不利な対戦カード。
articles.body:
Making tough lineup decisions each week can be the most challenging part of fantasy football. When you're torn between two similar players, start the player with the superior matchup.

But exactly how does one determine the best (and worst) weekly matchups?

The matchup rankings provide a schedule-independent method to evaluate positional matchups, ranking all 32 opposing defenses in order of most to least favorable for opposing players at all four skill positions. Instead of relying upon seasonal totals, we calibrate points-allowed data to show how each defense fared relative to the difficulty of the schedule it has faced. 

For Week 5, 2026 full-season data is used, and once five weeks are in the books, only the most recent five weeks' numbers will be used.

"Adj. FPA," or Adjusted Fantasy Points Allowed, reflects how far above or below players' weekly PPR fantasy point averages that defense held opponents at that position. A positive number means that the matchup is favorable; a negative number means it is unfavorable.

Finally, a caveat: Matchups are only one ingredient in my rankings formula. Not every favorable matchup should be exploited, nor unfavorable matchup avoided. If you want the most complete source for whom to start, consult our weekly rankings.

Quarterbacks

Matchups highlight: Jared Goff, Detroit Lions (at Arizona Cardinals). Lions games have been extremely conducive to big passing numbers. They've been involved in four of the nine games with the highest over/unders, with all of them going over, and they've run the fourth-most passing plays while allowing the second most. This is another of those lofty over/under games (54.5), and it involves a Cardinals defense that surrendered a combined 67.28 fantasy points on passing plays to Drew Lock, Brock Purdy and Jameis Winston the past three weeks. This might well be one of those games where scads of passing yardage piles up in the closing minutes.

Others to like:

Jacoby Brissett, Cardinals (versus Lions)

Matthew Stafford, Los Angeles Rams (versus Buffalo Bills, Monday Night Football)

Matchup to avoid: Brock Purdy, San Francisco 49ers (at Seattle Seahawks). The Seahawks, outside of their seemingly inexplicable 33-31 loss at home to Marcus Mariota and the Washington Commanders, have been a headache matchup for opposing quarterbacks. They held each of Drake Maye, Brissett and Justin Herbert under 10 fantasy points while creating seven total turnovers against them. Purdy himself struggled against the Seahawks in their two meetings last season, scoring 21.96 total fantasy points while committing three turnovers.

Running backs

Matchups highlight: D'Andre Swift, Chicago Bears (at Green Bay Packers). Kyle Monangai's Week 4 outburst casts the Bears' division of carries into question, but with Monangai exiting that game with a thumb injury, it might serve the team best to shift more of the work back to Swift, even if only for the week. articles.headline: Tottenham's Mathys Tel equals France under-21 goalscoring record
articles.description: Mathys Tel will be hoping to take his goal-scoring exploits with France Under-21s over the international break into Tottenham's fight to turn their Premier League season around.
articles.headlineJa: トッテナムのマティス・テル、フランスU-21の得点記録に並ぶ
articles.descriptionJa: マティス・テルは、代表ウィーク中のフランスU-21での得点感覚を、プレミアリーグのシーズン立て直しに向けたトッテナムの戦いに持ち込みたいと考えている。
articles.body:
Mathys Tel will be hoping to take his goal-scoring exploits with France Under-21s over the international break into Tottenham's fight to turn their Premier League season around.

Tel has yet to score for Spurs this season but hit a hat-trick in a 7-1 win over Switzerland in Orleans on Tuesday night as France, who had already qualified for the 2027 European U21 Championship, completed their group campaign unbeaten with eight victories.

With 17 goals, Tel, who also scored in two other games over the break, has equalled Odsonne Edouard's record for France U21s and could have put himself into contention for a senior call-up to Zinedine Zidane's squad for the Nations League games in November.

"My brother had been nagging me about it [the goals record] for months. In the end it was in the back of my mind," Tel told reporters, as quoted in L'Equipe.

"With qualification [achieved], there was a different kind of motivation that allowed me to give my best, so now I am very happy."

Roberto De Zerbi's Tottenham slumped to the bottom of the table ahead of the international break, with a 3-2 home defeat by Aston Villa a third loss from their five opening Premier League games.

The boss welcomed former player and first-team coach Gus Poyet to the training ground on Tuesday and appeared in good spirits as the pair chatted on the sidelines in a video on the club's social media account.

Spurs travel to Manchester United on Saturday and have a few fitness concerns following the international break.

Right-back Pedro Porro has been carrying a hamstring injury which saw him pull out the Spain squad ahead of the extended three-week window.

Defender Jan Paul van Hecke was then sent home early from the Netherlands camp with a foot problem, which could keep him out of contention at Old Trafford.

Fellow Dutchman Micky van de Ven picked up a minor hand injury after being accidentally stepped on during the win over Serbia in Eindhoven and was forced off late on, but the Spurs captain is expected to be involved.

Speaking after the match, Netherlands manager Xavi told reporters: "He is okay. He felt dizzy because he suffered with his finger. It is not a big injury."

articles.headline: Are Texans and Chargers this bad? And how do we bet the Rams one month in?
articles.description: Four weeks into the NFL season, what do we know, and what can we expect moving forward?
articles.headlineJa: テキサンズとチャージャーズはここまで弱いのか？シーズン開始1ヶ月、ラムズへの賭け方は？
articles.descriptionJa: NFLシーズン開始から4週間。これまでに判明したこと、そして今後の展望について。
articles.body:
Four weeks into the NFL season, the Houston Texans and Los Angeles Chargers are winless, a deeper stumble than anticipated. Which team can rebound, and which problems are real? The San Francisco 49ers look strong, as predicted, but is that start sustainable? Meanwhile, the Los Angeles Rams are Super Bowl favorites, yet their regular-season win total still offers a fade.

The Texans aren't this bad, the preseason thesis just cracked

Texans: 0-4, 0-4 ATS (45-1 to win Super Bowl, 18-1 entering Week 1)

The biggest preseason concern for Houston was whether the offense could finally complement an elite defense. Instead, the defense has become part of the problem. Houston is allowing 27 points per game after allowing 17 PPG last season. More concerning, the offseason investment in the run game hasn't translated. David Montgomery is averaging just 2.7 yards per carry, leaving C.J. Stroud responsible for creating most of the offense (again).

Stroud has actually been solid, throwing for 1,141 yards with five touchdowns and no interceptions. It's the lack of red zone execution -- top half of the league in attempts, bottom 10 in touchdowns scored. There's reason to expect improvement: Houston has essentially matched its opponents in total yardage, owns a positive turnover margin and has lost two games by four points or less. This looks more like an underperforming team than a terrible one.

The fix starts with the run game, even if that means leaning more on Woody Marks or adjusting the blocking approach rather than forcing Montgomery into something that isn't working. Defensively, Houston has to limit explosive passes; the pass rush is still getting home, so the secondary needs to capitalize on that pressure.

There's room for regression toward competence, but it shouldn't involve Stroud becoming Superman -- just play complementary football. Houston's season win total was 9.5 going into the season. At 0-4, the market has dropped them to 7.5. Seven wins is the new benchmark.

The Chargers lost their foundation before it ever had an identity

Chargers: 0-4, 0-3-1 ATS (100-1 to win Super Bowl, 17-1 entering Week 1)

The Chargers were a preseason regression candidate because last year's 11 wins were helped by a soft schedule and close-game success. The bad news: their 0-4 start goes beyond regression.

The offense Mike McDaniel was supposed to unlock has been undermined by the exact concern identified preseason: offensive line health. OT Rashawn Slater is doubtful, OT Joe Alt and G Trevor Penning are questionable, and C Tyler Biadasz is on injured reserve. Justin Herbert is pressing behind unstable protection, turning the ball over and failing to create explosive plays.

The defense has declined without coordinator Jesse Minter, though it has created opportunities, forcing five turnovers against Buffalo -- yet losing the game anyway. The fix is simplification: lean on Omarion Hampton and Keaton Mitchell, use motion and quicker throws, and stop asking Herbert

articles.headline: We don't get Man City guilty verdict without hacker Rui Pinto, but it doesn't make him a hero
articles.description: The Manchester City case, which has rocked English football to its core, wouldn't have been possible without Football Leaks and its founder, Rui Pinto. However, he is a complicated figure, with light and dark to his actions.
articles.headlineJa: ハッカーのルイ・ピントがいなければマン・シティの有罪判決はなかったが、彼がヒーローなわけではない
articles.descriptionJa: イングランドのサッカー界を根底から揺るがしているマンチェスター・シティの事案は、「フットボール・リークス」とその創設者ルイ・ピントがいなければ不可能だっただろう。しかし、彼の行動には光と影があり、複雑な人物である。
articles.body:
It's worth reminding ourselves that the Manchester City case, which has rocked English football to its foundation, would never have seen the light of day without a spiky-haired college dropout turned self-taught hacker named Rui Pinto.

Had he not obtained and shared more than 70 million documents with the German magazine Der Spiegel starting in 2016, culminating in the publication of their massive "Football Leaks" investigation two years later, there would have been no investigation of City -- not by UEFA, not by the Premier League, not by any of the other bodies that may get involved once the current process is concluded.

Simply put, there would have been no legal basis for anyone to do this. We would have had an alternate reading of history -- one where City get new owners, Abu Dhabi United Group in 2009, spend a ton of money, watch their revenues skyrocket and dominate the game, all the while complying with every single financial regulation set before them. (The only exception was in 2014, when they breached UEFA's Financial Fair Play regulations and eventually signed a three-year settlement agreement.)

Whatever the ultimate outcome of the City case -- whether it results in expulsion from the Premier League and Sheikh Mansour having to shell out hundreds of millions in fines and compensation, or somehow ends in the club getting most, if not all, of the charges overturned on appeal -- this should be a massive wake-up call to those running the game. The message: football needs better oversight and more transparency.

Whichever way the dust settles, this much is obvious: the system failed. Either City did participate in a massive "sham" (to quote from the verdict), effectively cheating while the system failed to notice and act, or the Premier League is so inept that it has somehow been duped by a conspiracy of legacy clubs into conducting an ultimately futile eight-year investigation. Neither outcome is good; in fact, both are embarrassingly bad for the world's most successful league.

What would better oversight and transparency look like? How about something like we have in the NFL, where information about salaries, sponsorships and other revenue is shared not just with the league, but with teams around the league itself as well as the players' union. That creates a virtuous cycle of self-policing and makes it much harder to engage in financial skullduggery. (Harder, but not impossible, as old-school San Francisco 49ers fans will confirm.)

In the Premier League, far too much is a closely guarded secret in the name of "competitive advantage" -- clubs, not just City, disclose as little as legally allowed as if they were running some normal business, not a hugely important public trust like the world's most popular sport.

All of which brings us back to Pinto.

articles.headline: Basketball Power Index: NBA projections, playoff chances for 2026-27 season
articles.description: ESPN's Basketball Power Index projections for the 2026-27 NBA season are out, including a ranking of all 30 teams.
articles.headlineJa: バスケットボール・パワー・インデックス：2026-27年NBAシーズンの展望とプレーオフ進出の可能性
articles.descriptionJa: ESPNによる2026-27年NBAシーズンのバスケットボール・パワー・インデックスの予測が発表され、全30チームのランキングが公開された。
articles.body:
The NBA season starts Tuesday, Oct. 20, and ESPN has multiple previews to guide readers, including a ranking of the top 100 players, a look at the top players in new places and capsules on each team, with the most important stats that affect teams' win-loss records.

Now it's time for a season preview using ESPN's Basketball Power Index (BPI), which evaluates two different strength measures for all 30 NBA teams: one based on players currently available, and the other based on players who should be available during the playoffs. Then, to create preseason projections, the BPI takes into account win totals from the betting market in conjunction with each team's schedule and other factors, simulating the season thousands of times, with the results forming these projections.

Once the season begins, the BPI watches what happens in games and updates both its current BPI and its playoff BPI. There are numerous benefits to this, particularly that it adjusts game predictions on the fly when there are reports of players missing games. If Giannis Antetokounmpo is going to miss a game, for instance, the BPI marks down the Miami Heat's chance to win that game by an amount suggested by history. Sometimes, those injury reports are late or inaccurate (ahem, Joel Embiid) and it annoys us, the BPI and the league as a whole. But don't hold that against the BPI's model.

One thing the BPI isn't seeing this season is a secret prediction edge over Las Vegas. There aren't major deviations in this model's rankings from what Vegas is forecasting.

Let's dig into the projections, including how it ranks teams from 1 to 30 and which teams have the best chance to win the NBA Finals.

Jump to a section:

1-30 team rankings

NBA playoff projections

NBA Finals projections

More takeaways

Regular-season projections

The BPI values shown are the current numbers, not the version for the playoffs. The Golden State Warriors are down at No. 20, reflecting the absence of Jimmy Butler III, who tore his ACL in January and could return around midseason. The Warriors would be No. 12 if they were at full strength.

There is only one other team with an injury causing significant deviations between their current and playoff power: Embiid and the Philadelphia 76ers. That's because we know from history Embiid is going to miss games -- he has played 41 games per season since he was drafted and has played just 96 over the past three seasons -- and he is a good enough player that it matters. With Embiid, the Sixers have the third-best playoff BPI, consistent with the expectation they are among the favorites to come out of the East.

There are a few things to note from the overall league rankings. First, the Denver Nuggets finished last season as the league's best offense in the league, and the BPI isn't going to argue that they got worse. They've been in the top six on offense for seven years now. They're, of course, led by Nikola Jokic, who was the No. 1-ranked player in our top 100.

articles.headline: Early 2026 NFL trends for the 49ers, Vikings, Bucs, Texans, Giants, Browns
articles.description: Just how good are the 49ers? Are the Texans and Bucs better than their records? Are the Giants and Browns worse? We put the NFL season's first month in historical context.
articles.descriptionJa: 49ersはどれほど強いのか？ TexansとBucsは戦績以上に好調なのか？ GiantsとBrownsはそれ以上に低迷しているのか？ NFLシーズンの最初の1か月を歴史的背景から分析する。
articles.body:
Early in every NFL season, you hear a lot about the pace of certain stats. But most of the time when you see that a player or team is on pace to record a certain stat, you have no idea about issues for similar things in the past.

Performance is usually going to regress toward the mean. Teams and players that started superhot will cool. Teams and players that were terrible early will get better. So we don't want to compare a team's performance after four games to what other teams have done over 16- and 17-game seasons. We want to compare that performance to what others have done in the same number of games.

We can do that with DVOA (defense-adjusted value over average) stats. We've gone back and rerun every season since 1977 to see what DVOA would have looked like as of Week 4. Here, teams are rated solely based on what they did through four games (and what opponents did over that time). And every year of DVOA is normalized so that we're comparing teams to the averages of their own era, not to what teams do in today's game.

This year, there's one team in particular playing at a historical level. You might not realize quite how good the San Francisco 49ers have been. But will their usual spate of injuries prevent them from living up to their September greatness with the franchise's sixth Super Bowl title? Let's look closer and explore three other early trends that I've noticed in the DVOA data.

1. The 49ers are the 11th-best team overall through four games since 1977 (and have the third-best passing offense)

The 49ers shocked everyone when they not only beat the favored Rams in Week 1 but destroyed them. We've sort of written off that Rams performance because of the whole jetlag issue, but maybe a part of the 49ers winning was being really good?

San Francisco has continued to win games, mostly decisively. It dominated the Dolphins in Week 2 and had a big fourth quarter to beat the Broncos in Week 4. The Niners' Week 3 victory over Arizona was 36-30, but a play-by-play breakdown suggests the 49ers outplayed the Cardinals by a much wider margin. They outgained the Cards 8.7 yards to 4.5 yards per play but had 31 fewer plays. The efficiency predicts future performance better than the raw number of plays.

Put it all together, and the 49ers are No. 1 in my DVOA ratings with a historically high number. Only 10 teams since 1977 have been higher through the first four games.

The 49ers' success is primarily being driven by their superb passing game, with quarterback Brock Purdy leading the league in QBR. Sure, the 49ers rank fifth in defensive DVOA and ninth in run offense, but the passing game is historically good. Since 1977, the only teams with a better passing game through four games were the 1998 Broncos with John Elway and a shockingly strong 1999 Washington team with Brad Johnson at quarterback. articles.headline: NFL Week 5 latest intel, buzz questions, news, fantasy tips: What we're hearing
articles.description: Could injuries to Saquon Barkley, Lamar Jackson and others derail their teams? Which AFC teams should trade for a WR? Which coordinators could get head coach interest?
articles.headlineJa: NFL第5週の最新情報、噂、ニュース、ファンタジー・チップス：今、何が話題か
articles.descriptionJa: サクオン・バークレーやラマー・ジャクソンらの負傷は、チームの勢いを削ぐことになるのか？ AFCのどのチームがWR（ワイドレシーバー）を獲得すべきか？ どのコーディネーターがヘッドコーチの関心を集めるのか？
articles.body:
It's already Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season! Insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano have been making calls to sources around the league for the latest news and notable buzz.

Injuries are starting to pile up as we hit the quarter mark of the season, and a few important players went down Sunday, including Lamar Jackson, Pat Surtain II, Ja'Marr Chase and Saquon Barkley. Which teams could be in trouble if they have to go without one of their stars? And which teams might have to make a trade sooner rather than later to either replace an injured player or quickly fix a weak spot in the roster? The trade deadline is approaching fast -- it is under five weeks out.

Coaches are also under the microscope with four weeks of games behind us. Are any seats warming around the league? And have any coordinators shown enough in the early going to put themselves on the radar for head coach interviews if they keep this up? It's all here, as Jeremy and Dan answer big questions, hand out useful fantasy football nuggets and empty their reporting notebooks heading into Week 5.

Jump to:

Warming seats | Rising coordinators

Fantasy football advice

Which player's Week 4 injury could be most detrimental to his team?

Graziano: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is the obvious answer if he has to miss time (which we don't know for sure yet). They're just so different without him. Having him on the field makes things easier for running back Derrick Henry, whereas defenses can lock in on Henry when they don't have to fear the QB run.

Fowler: Can't understate that one. The Ravens are hopeful he won't miss time, but this week feels uncertain. I'll go with Broncos corner Pat Surtain II, who is set to miss multiple weeks with an ankle injury. With Denver's offense struggling to consistently score points, it needs the defense to reestablish its dominant form. But after ripping through the league with 68 sacks last season, the Broncos have eight through four games ... which heightens the importance of having a former Defensive Player of the Year such as Surtain in the secondary. Normally I would go with the star quarterback who's hurt, but Surtain's absence could have a sizable ripple effect for a team on the ropes.

Graziano: A Saquon Barkley absence could exacerbate the Eagles' problems. I know Barkley isn't having the best season, but the Philadelphia offense is getting really low on good players. It had to play Sunday without right tackle Lane Johnson (who has since retired), top wide receiver DeVonta Smith and, other than the first four plays, Barkley. It's a thin group around Jalen Hurts right now, and even at full strength it was trying to figure out a new offense under a first-time playcaller. If the Eagles are going to pull out of this, they're going to need as many of their stars as close to full strength as possible.

articles.headline: Why Jaguars play 26 of next 30 regular-season games away from Jacksonville
articles.description: The Jaguars will become the first NFL team since 1926 to play in 12 or more stadiums in a single season -- including Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: なぜジャガーズは、レギュラーシーズン残り30試合のうち26試合をジャクソンビル以外で戦うのか
articles.descriptionJa: ジャガーズは、今週日曜日のトッテナム・ホットスパー・スタジアムでの試合を含め、1シーズンで12以上のスタジアムを使用する、1926年以来初のNFLチームとなる。
articles.body:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Jaguars cornerback Jourdan Lewis likes to go bird-watching when his team is playing on the road.

He'll do it from inside the team bus when it pulls up to the opponent's stadium, and he doesn't have to look too long to find one. He doesn't need a field guide to identify the type, either.

"I love seeing the fans pull up middle fingers and flip the bird at us," Lewis said. "It gets the juices flowing."

He had better get used to seeing that regularly, because the Jaguars aren't going to be spending much time at EverBank Stadium over the next 23 months. They'll play just four of the next 30 regular-season games in Jacksonville, a stretch necessitated by the $1.4 billion renovation to their stadium that is forcing the Jaguars to play 2027 home games in Orlando at Camping World Stadium, a two-hour drive south.

As daunting as that odyssey might be, the Jaguars aren't grumbling about it. They've embraced it and turned it into a slogan: Anywhere, anytime, anybody.

"We're not going to use it as an excuse," Jacksonville coach Liam Coen said. "It is what it is, and our mindset and mentality is going to be: Drop us off on a plane anywhere and we'll go play you."

By the time the 2026 regular season ends, the Jaguars will become the first NFL team since the Duluth Eskimos in 1926 to play in 12 or more stadiums in a single season. The Eskimos from Minnesota had just one home game that campaign and played in 14 stadiums. The Jaguars will play in 12 stadiums in 2026 -- not including any potential away playoff games -- with seven of their final 10 contests on the road.

The Jaguars beat the New England Patriots 35-6 at home on Sept. 27, and the next time they'll play there will be Nov. 1 against the Indianapolis Colts. That 34-day break is allowing for -- weather permitting -- uninterrupted work on EverBank Stadium. The Jaguars and the city of Jacksonville are splitting the cost of the renovation (team owner Shad Khan is responsible for all cost overruns), and work began following the team's playoff loss to the Buffalo Bills in January.

International games are a significant part of the Jaguars' pilgrimage -- starting this week. They leave Thursday for London (approximately a nine-hour flight) to play back-to-back designated home games against the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Sunday (9:30 a.m. ET, NFL Network) and the Houston Texans on Oct. 18 at Wembley Stadium (9:30 a.m. ET, NFL Network). Those will be the 15th and 16th games the franchise has played in London dating back to the 2013 season. No other NFL team has played more than eight international games (Bills).

When the Jaguars face Philadelphia, Jacksonville punter Logan Cooke will play in his NFL-record 10th international game, breaking a tie with former Jags offensive lineman Tyler Shatley. It's a record that Cooke said really means one thing: He has been around a long time for a team that makes regular trips to play games out of the country.

articles.headline: Texans' defense has gone from elite to struggling to close out games
articles.description: Houston has given up late leads in three of the first four games despite scoring go-ahead touchdowns.
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- The season opened with Super Bowl hopes for the Houston Texans, but after four weeks, hopes of even making the playoffs seem grim.

The Texans are at 0-4 and for various reasons: Some weeks the blame lies on the offense; other weeks it's the defense; some weeks it' both.

Simply put, Houston has not lived up to expectations internally or externally.

Last year, the Texans started 0-3 and had a fierce turnaround towards the playoffs, and in 2023, they started 0-2 and had the same result.

But only one team in NFL history has overcome a 0-4 start: The 1992 Chargers.

Previous success stories don't matter to quarterback C.J. Stroud as he said following the loss to the Dallas Cowboys last Sunday, "last year's bread isn't going to feed us this year."

"You have to be an iPhone. You have to upgrade every year," Stroud said. "You have to upgrade whatever that looks like from personnel to plays to execution. Everything has to rise up and you can't look back and be like, 'Oh, well, we did it this time, we can do it this time.' You have to be able to flush successes and failures and be able to do your job each and every play. It doesn't matter what happened in the previous year."

The most unforeseen downgrade is the defense, that allowed the fewest yards and second-fewest points last season, not playing up to its potential. So far its allowed 34 points to the Cowboys and 36 against the Buffalo Bills in the season opener. For context, no one scored over 30 against the Texans last season.

The last time a team eclipsed that mark was on Christmas in 2024 when the Baltimore Ravens scored 31.

The defense had a players-only meeting after Week 2, but All-Pro defensive end Will Anderson Jr. said there needs to action behind the words after the most-recent loss.

"It's only so much talking you can do," Anderson said. "Now it's time to look at yourself in the mirror as a man and figure out where your priorities are and how you are going to show up and get it fixed."

Stroud entered the season under heavy scrutiny after a litany of mistakes (five interceptions and two fumbles) in Houston's two-game playoff run in January and two down seasons compared to his historic rookie year in 2023.

Through the first four weeks, Stroud ranks sixth in passing yards (1,141) and is sixth in explosive rate on his drop backs, per Next Gen Stats.

But more importantly, he and the offense have given the team chances to win. Three of their four losses have come after scoring a go-ahead touchdown late in the fourth quarter.

"If the offense goes out and plays like they played to give us 30 points, defensively you have to find a way to close that game out," coach DeMeco Ryans said. "It was disappointing that we've been in three games ... where the offense has done a great job and we haven't been able to close it out there in the second half. We've got to look at it all and see what changes we need to make and what we need to fix."

articles.body:
After an investigation spanning years, Manchester City were found guilty on more than 100 charges of serious breaches of Premier League financial regulations. The decision is a major development in one of the biggest scandals in soccer history, but the saga is far from over.

What happens next? What does the ruling mean for England's dominant force over the past decade, its fans and its players? ESPN's writers have you covered on every angle, from transfer implications to the mood at City's rival clubs.

Check back here for the latest as this story continues to unfold.

O'Hanlon: Mock draft: How would Premier League teams pick if Man City cheating scandal took a turn?

Four clubs (Arsenal, Liverpool, Man United and Tottenham) retained their legal rights in the Premier League's case against Man City. Now that a guilty verdict has been issued, what will they do in response?

Ogden: How a mass Man City player exodus would warp the transfer market

If Manchester City are punished by being relegated from the Premier League, group of players worth more than £1 billion in transfer fees would suddenly become available.

Dawson: How Man City players, staff are handling Premier League verdict

As the reaction to Man City's guilty verdict continues to ripple across the sporting world, the club's internal messaging is very much one of confidence and carrying on. That might be easier said than done.

Olley: Manchester City guilty charges explained: Premier League's options, how appeal works

Man City's guilty verdict is a landmark moment. But what comes next? What punishments are on the table, and how does the appeals process work?

Ogden: Does Man City's guilty verdict impact Guardiola's legacy as an all-time coaching great?

Pep Guardiola won 16 major honors as Man City manager. They all now count for nothing after the Premier League found the club guilty of systematically breaking financial rules.

Marcotti: Hard to see how Man City recover from extraordinary guilty verdict

The confirmation that Manchester City were found guilty by the Premier League on over 100 breaches of financial regulations has sent shock waves through the sport. How do Man City survive this?

Dawson: Man City's guilt the talk of the town around English soccer

Man City being found guilty of 100-plus charges by the Premier League was the only topic of conversation around Manchester, and lower-league games, in the first weekend of action since the verdict.

Ogden: Man City verdict will leave a stain and stench on a Premier League era

Manchester City have been found guilty of almost all 115 financial charges against them. It means an era of English soccer is now tarnished with multiple asterisks.
